title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: custom engine agents for DoD users
notes: claim 67: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing promises that nothing reaches users before a developer builds an agent, although its default state is not documented. It also understates direct hosting and model costs, leaves a documented DoD Toolkit restriction open, and presents SDK-specific limitations as applying to every custom engine agent.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The roadmap item and service description disagree about DoD availability of neighboring agent types.
claims.quote: "description": "Users in DoD will be able to use custom engine agents."
claims.fix: Replace the disagreement sentence with: 'The roadmap item covers custom engine agents, while the service description lists Declarative agents and Agent Builder as not currently available in DoD; these are different agent types.' claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Cost is low, although the deciding costs are the builder's orchestration, models and hosting.
claims.quote: cost: "low"; rationale: "the cost it names is the builder's own orchestration, models and hosting". The standard defines low as "indirect cost only: admin time, communications, training", not paid hosting or model consumption.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with: 'Variable. Builders must budget for their own orchestration, models and hosting, with costs depending on the selected Azure AI Foundry, App Service or Azure AI Bot Service resources. A DoD-specific price is not yet published.' Keep the cost page citation and do not invent a DoD credit rate.

claims.where: rationale: impact
claims.claim: Only developers who build an agent and the users they share it with notice this change.
claims.quote: Searched: custom engine agents available automatically deployed default new agents DoD tenant. Read overview, comparison, agent-installation and agent-actions excerpts; none limits everyone affected to builders and their sharing recipients, and organizational/store distribution is documented.
claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with: 'Low. The likely impact is a small group choosing to build or use an agent; Microsoft has not stated that an agent appears in DoD tenants on its own.' This expresses the rating as analysis without asserting an exhaustive affected-user list.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The governance checklist tells readers to review stored prompts and responses through Content Search or Purview, but the table has no corresponding control.
claims.quote: After rollout: "Review stored prompts and responses with Content Search or Microsoft Purview". The controls table has only the agent Block action.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist step 'Review stored prompts and responses with Content Search or Microsoft Purview, the route Learn gives for custom engine agent data.' Retain the supported background statement in Risk assessment; do not add an unverified control row.
